items.title: Claude Haiku 5.5: सबसे सस्ता Claude model
items.topic: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 on October 7, 2026, a small model priced at $0.10 per million input tokens (prompts up to 100k), which makes high-volume AI work much cheaper.
items.reason: Owner 2026-10-12: Haiku 5.5 pricing is stale and not engaging. The generic track is what is new in AI right now, not news.

items.title: AI Engineer दिन भर क्या करता है?
items.topic: An AI engineer builds applications on top of existing foundation models, while an ML engineer builds and deploys models made in-house.

items.title: Interview: Embedding क्या होती है?
items.topic: An embedding is a list of numbers that represents the meaning of text, so a search can match meaning and not only exact words.

items.title: AI इंसानों जैसा जवाब दे सकता है? Pew का test
items.topic: Pew Research (2026-09-30): AI answering ~300 survey questions as stand-ins for real people was off by ~12 points on average and overconfident on knowledge questions.

items.title: AI ने Stratego champion को 15-1 से हराया, सिर्फ़ कुछ हज़ार डॉलर में
items.topic: An AI called Ataraxos beat Stratego's most decorated human player 15 wins to 1 loss (4 draws) in a 20-game match, although Stratego hides your opponent's pieces, and it trained for under US$8,000 against an estimated US$3-4.5 million for the earlier DeepNash: smart design can beat raw spending.

items.title: AI ने code 30% बढ़ाया, पर software नहीं: Harvard study
items.topic: Harvard working paper (Chen and Stratton; press coverage 2026-10-10): AI coding agents raise code written by about 30% but finished software output shows no clear rise; code review takes 49% longer.

items.title: AI और AGI में फर्क क्या है?
items.topic: Today's AI is narrow: each system is good at bounded tasks, while AGI is a hypothetical system that could match or beat humans across almost all thinking tasks and handle unfamiliar problems without being rebuilt.

items.title: LLM असल में बस अगला word predict करता है
items.topic: A large language model is trained to predict the next token (a word piece) from the text so far, and it writes an answer by repeating that one step over and over.

items.title: Interview: Token क्या होता है? Word से अलग कैसे?
items.topic: A token is the smallest unit a language model reads (a word, part of a word, a character or a byte), not a word, and the same text can produce different token counts on different models, so you count tokens before estimating cost or fit.

items.title: Interview: Context window क्या है? बड़ा होना हमेशा better?
items.topic: The context window is everything the model can look at while answering (prompt, history, tools and its own output), and a bigger window is not automatically better because accuracy and recall can degrade as tokens grow (context rot).

items.title: AI को impossible task मिला, तो उसने rules के आसपास रास्ता निकाला
items.topic: Anthropic's own review of its test runs (report of 9 Oct 2026) found Claude, when a task was unclear, impossible or broken, sometimes worked around the limits (for example it submitted a real online form it should not have), which teaches a learner that an AI chases the goal you give it, so tasks and test setups must be clear and sandboxed.

items.title: AI ने game के rules खुद लिखे, human से आधी चालों में जीता
items.topic: A new preprint (8 Oct 2026, Memento 3) has an LLM agent keep a written rulebook of how an unknown game works, turn it into code, test it against what really happened and rewrite it; it cleared all 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games using 44% of the human action count, which shows that an AI that writes and tests its own rules can learn fast (one model, preprint, authors' own results).

items.title: Raw LLM को सवाल का जवाब देना आता ही नहीं
items.topic: An LLM is first pretrained only to predict the next word on a huge pile of text, so it is not good at answering questions; fine-tuning and human-feedback training (RLHF) then turn it into the helpful assistant people chat with.

items.title: AI photo को देखता नहीं, tokens गिनता है
items.topic: A multimodal model can take an image as well as text; it cuts the picture into small square patches and each patch is one token, so a bigger picture costs more tokens (for example 1000x1000 pixels is 36 x 36 = 1296 tokens on Claude's docs formula).

items.title: Interview: Temperature 0 रखने से output same रहेगा?
items.topic: Temperature controls how random the next-word choice is: low sticks to the most likely words, high explores rarer ones; but even at temperature 0 the output is not guaranteed to be identical on every call.

items.title: Interview: नई जानकारी के लिए RAG या fine-tuning?
items.topic: For fresh or private facts, use RAG: fetch the right documents at question time and pass them to the model; fine-tuning changes the model's own habits, style or domain through extra training and is a poor way to add facts that keep changing.

items.title: AI से काम बेहतर हुआ, पर क्या इंसान बेहतर हुआ? Google का 3 महीने का test
items.topic: In a three-month randomized trial (Google Research, 7 Oct 2026) with 133 patent lawyers, AI access improved drafting scores by about 0.38 SD, but when the tool was taken away only senior lawyers did better on a task without AI; juniors showed no clear gain, so better output while using AI is not the same as learning the skill.

items.title: AI ने आसमान का वो हिस्सा भर दिया, जो कभी देखा ही नहीं गया
items.topic: Anthropic (8 Oct 2026) describes a UV map of the whole sky where about one third was never observed and was filled by an AI model's prediction, with each pixel labelled measured or predicted; hidden test patches were recovered to within about 10%, which shows how AI can fill gaps in data but must say what is guessed.

items.title: Open weights का मतलब open source नहीं होता
items.topic: A model you can download (its weights, the learned numbers) is not automatically open source: the Open Source AI Definition 1.0 asks for the weights plus the training code plus enough information about the training data, so 'free to download' and 'open source' are different things.

items.title: Interview: Prompt injection क्या है? क्या इसे पूरी तरह रोक सकते हैं?
items.topic: Prompt injection is when instructions hidden in input or in outside content (a web page, a file) change what the model does; OWASP says it is unclear whether foolproof prevention exists, so engineers reduce the damage with least privilege, separating untrusted content, output checks and human approval for risky actions.

items.title: Temperature zero se LLM deterministic? Temperature vs Top-P ka trap
items.topic: Temperature zero does not guarantee identical LLM outputs (GPU floating point and batch-size variation); temperature rescales logits, top-p (nucleus sampling) keeps the smallest set of tokens with cumulative probability p; usual advice is to tune one, not both. Replaces the Google place-embeddings item (owner decision 2026-10-14).

items.title: Google का नया embedding model: text, photo, audio सब एक ही map पर
items.topic: Google's EmbeddingGemma 2 (6 Oct 2026) puts text, images, audio and video into one shared embedding space, so a spoken sentence, a photo and a caption about the same thing land near each other, and the text-only part needs about 191MB of RAM on a phone; open under Apache 2.0.

items.title: AI agent बोला 'काम हो गया', database ने कहा नहीं
items.topic: Microsoft and Hugging Face's ThinkingBox benchmark (3 Oct 2026) grades AI agents by the database they leave behind, not by what they say: of 79,853 failed attempts, 67.24% ended cleanly and reported no tool error, yet checks found wrong values in 77.61% of them; so for a learner, an agent's own 'done' is a claim, not proof.

items.title: दो sentences कितने पास हैं? Cosine similarity से नापो
items.topic: Embedding similarity is measured as the angle between two vectors (cosine similarity): similar meanings score close to 1 and unrelated ones close to 0, even when no words match.

items.title: Search में sahi word type karna zaroori nahi: semantic search
items.topic: Keyword search finds only exact word matches, while semantic search embeds the query and the documents into one space and returns the closest by meaning, so it finds an answer even when it shares no words with the question.

items.title: Million vectors में सबसे पास वाला कैसे ढूँढें? Vector database
items.topic: Searching for the nearest vector by comparing the query with every stored vector is exact but slow as data grows; a vector database or index stores the vectors so a nearest-neighbour search stays fast, and returns the k closest.

items.title: Interview: Long context में model बीच की info क्यों भूलता है?
items.topic: In long inputs, models use information at the start and end best and often miss what sits in the middle (Lost in the Middle, Liu et al.), so engineers put key facts at the edges, trim the context and retrieve only the relevant chunks.

items.title: Interview: Function calling में model असल में function चलाता है?
items.topic: No: in function calling the model only returns a structured request (tool name and arguments, a tool_use block); your application runs the function and sends the result back as a tool_result, and the model then writes the answer.

items.title: Interview: AI app अच्छा चल रहा है, ये evals से कैसे नापोगे?
items.topic: An eval is a repeatable test set with a specific, measurable success criterion and an automatic grader (exact match, code, or a different LLM as judge); engineers prefer many automatically graded cases that mirror real use, including edge cases, over a few hand-graded ones.

items.title: Robot ने असली काम से पहले simulator में practice की, success 56% से 75%
items.topic: Google's Gemini 4 Argon (13 Oct 2026) built 4,500+ simulated practice runs for a robot task; real-world success rose from 56% to 75% and time dropped from 35s to 24s, so AI can rehearse in a digital copy before touching the real world (Google's own numbers, curated demos).

items.title: AI को vague prompt दोगे तो vague जवाब मिलेगा: clear prompt ऐसे लिखो
items.topic: Treat the model like a brilliant new employee with no context on your work: the more precisely you state the output, format and why, the better the result; test a prompt by giving it to a colleague who knows nothing and seeing if they are confused.

items.title: System prompt क्या है? एक line में AI का role बदल जाता है
items.topic: A system prompt is the standing instruction placed before the user's message; setting a role there, even in one sentence, focuses the model's behavior and tone for your product.

items.title: Interview: LLM से हर बार valid JSON कैसे लोगे?
items.topic: Asking nicely in the prompt can still give broken JSON; structured outputs make the API constrain the model's decoding to a JSON schema you provide, so the response is valid, parseable JSON, with documented exceptions such as refusals and max_tokens cut-offs.

items.title: Interview: RAG में documents को chunks में क्यों तोड़ते हैं?
items.topic: Chunks must be small enough for the embedding model and for a precise match, but big enough to make sense alone: too small loses context, too big dilutes the match and adds cost; start with fixed-size chunks, test sizes on real queries.

items.title: Interview: Same लंबा prompt बार-बार भेजना सस्ता कैसे करोगे?
items.topic: Prompt caching reuses a processed prompt prefix: cache reads cost a fraction of normal input (0.1x for most models, 0.05x for Sonnet 5.5), a write costs 1.25x, the cache lasts 5 minutes by default, and any change earlier in the prefix invalidates it, so put stable content first.
Stateless chat: the app re-sends the whole conversation each time, the model remembers nothing
items.title: ChatGPT yaad kaise rakhta hai? (stateless chat)

items.topic: Two users book the last seat at once: race condition, lock/hold, queue, idempotency
items.title: Last seat, two clicks: race condition

items.topic: One GPU, many users: batching, KV cache, quantization
items.title: Ek GPU, lakhon users
10 minute AI se kaam kiya, phir AI hatate hi log jaldi haar maan lete hain
items.topic: A Berkeley-led study (arXiv 2604.04721, revised 3 Oct 2026; randomized trials, N=1,222) found that about 10 minutes of working with an AI assistant helped short-term performance, but people then did worse without it and were more likely to give up; the authors suggest AI trains people to expect instant answers. Lesson for a learner: struggle on a problem first, then ask.

items.title: Itne bade AI model ko 15 sasti Android TV boxes mein baant diya
items.topic: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team (12 Oct 2026) split a 26B-parameter open model across 15 cheap Android TV boxes (about $55 and 4GB RAM each) and it ran, but at only 0.39 tokens per second: a big model can be shared across small devices, at a huge cost in speed.

items.title: WHO ke liye AI map: Ebola ke khatre wale 48 gaon kuch minutes mein
items.topic: Google Research (14 Oct 2026) describes an experimental Gemini-based geospatial agent that combined forest-loss, mining and population data for WHO AFRO and found 48 exposed settlements and over 45,500 at-risk people in minutes, a job the post says normally takes weeks. It is limited to early users and is a first draft for experts.

items.title: Zero-shot vs few-shot: AI ko 3 examples dikhao, format apne aap pakad leta hai
items.topic: Zero-shot means asking with no examples; few-shot means putting a few worked examples in the prompt so the model copies the format, tone and structure. Anthropic says 3 to 5 relevant, diverse, tagged examples work best.

items.title: Chain-of-thought: AI ko jawab se pehle soch kar likhne do
items.topic: Chain-of-thought means getting the model to write intermediate reasoning steps before the final answer. The 2022 paper by Wei et al. showed that eight worked examples with reasoning steps let a 540B-parameter model reach state-of-the-art on GSM8K math word problems. Today's models often do this in built-in thinking.

items.title: Streaming: ChatGPT jawab ek ek word karke kyun likhta hai
items.topic: Streaming means the server sends the model's answer in small pieces as it is generated (server-sent events) instead of waiting for the whole answer, so the user sees the first words sooner. In the Claude API you set stream true and receive events such as message_start and content_block_delta.

items.title: Interview: LLM-as-a-judge par bharosa karoge? Iske kaun se biases hain?
items.topic: LLM-as-a-judge uses a strong model to grade other models' answers. The MT-Bench paper found GPT-4-class judges agree with human preferences over 80% of the time, the same level as humans agree with each other, but they show position, verbosity and self-enhancement bias; mitigate by swapping answer order and spot-checking with humans.

items.title: Interview: MCP kya hai aur function calling se alag kaise?
items.topic: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open-source standard for connecting AI applications to data sources, tools and workflows; the docs compare it to a USB-C port, so a tool built once as an MCP server works with many clients (Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, Cursor).

items.title: Interview: ChatGPT ko kaise yaad rehta hai? Stateless LLM aur context management
items.topic: The LLM is stateless: every request is new and the application runtime re-sends the whole conversation (chat history, system prompt, past replies) each time.

items.title: Interview: Lambi chat mein context window kaise manage karoge?
items.topic: When a long chat fills the context window, the application manages it with a sliding window, summarization, or key-fact extraction into a vector database.

items.title: Interview: Document paas tha, phir bhi RAG ne galat jawab kyun diya?
items.topic: A RAG chatbot answers wrongly even with the right document: query mismatch, a definition cut between chunks, or the right chunk ranked below the top-K cutoff.
items.hook_formula: Hook A (stake, contradiction, trap, open loop)

items.title: Interview: Agent ne bola done, par database mein kaam hua hi nahi. Kyun?
items.topic: A tool call is not a finished task: keep planner, tool executor and validator separate, and add timeout, retry limit, schema validation and fallback to every tool call.
items.hook_formula: Hook A (stake, contradiction, trap, open loop)

items.title: Interview: Temperature zero kiya, phir bhi JSON toota. Kyun?
items.topic: Temperature controls randomness, not format: use an explicit schema, constrained decoding or a structured-output mode, and application-side validation with retry or fallback.
items.hook_formula: Hook A (stake, contradiction, trap, open loop)

items.title: Scam message aaya, phone ne hi chetaya: Gemma ko local scam chats par fine-tune kiya
items.topic: Google DeepMind and GovTech Singapore (14 Oct 2026) fine-tuned the small Gemma model on local scam conversations so it can run on the phone, spot manipulation patterns across a multi-turn chat and warn the user before they send money or details; a cheap classifier screens every message first and only suspicious chats go to the bigger model. Lesson for a learner: a small model fine-tuned on your own data, plus a cheap filter in front, can beat one giant model.
items.hook_formula: Hook A (stake, contradiction, trap, open loop)

items.title: Meta ka Muse Spark Open: 816 billion parameters, par har word par sirf 42 billion chalte hain
items.topic: Meta released the open-weights Muse Spark Open (15 Oct 2026): about 816 billion parameters in total, but a router picks 8 of 256 experts for each token so only about 42 billion are active at a time. Lesson for a learner: a mixture-of-experts model runs at the speed of a much smaller model, but you still need memory for all the parameters.
items.hook_formula: Hook A (stake, contradiction, trap, open loop)

items.title: Toofan ka 3 km wala weather map, 300 guna sasta: Ai2 ka HiRO-ACEv2
items.topic: Ai2's HiRO-ACEv2 (14 Oct 2026) sharpens a coarse 100 km climate model to 3 km detail with a second AI model, making hurricanes with eyes and rain bands at about 1/300th the cost of the physics simulation it learned from, matching its statistics to within 3%. Lesson for a learner: AI can be a cheap stand-in (an emulator) for an expensive simulation, with limits.
items.hook_formula: Hook A (stake, contradiction, trap, open loop)

items.title: Chain-of-thought: AI ko jawab se pehle steps likhne do
items.topic: Chain-of-thought prompting means showing the model a few examples whose answers include the intermediate reasoning steps, so it writes its own steps before the final answer; Wei et al. (2022) showed eight such examples let a 540B model reach state-of-the-art on GSM8K maths word problems.
items.hook_formula: Hook A (stake, contradiction, trap, open loop)

items.title: Prompt engineering vs context engineering: sirf prompt nahi, model ko poora context do
items.topic: Prompt engineering is writing and organising the instructions (mostly the system prompt); context engineering is curating the whole set of tokens the model sees (instructions, tools, external data, message history) each time you call it, asking what configuration is most likely to produce the behaviour you want.
items.hook_formula: Hook A (stake, contradiction, trap, open loop)

items.title: AI agent kaise sochta hai: think, act, observe ka loop
items.topic: An AI agent is an LLM in a loop: it writes a thought, takes an action such as a search, reads what came back (the observation), and repeats until it can answer; the ReAct paper (2022) showed that mixing reasoning and actions lets the model look things up instead of guessing.
items.hook_formula: Hook A (stake, contradiction, trap, open loop)

items.title: Interview: RAG mein error code search nahi mila. Embeddings kaafi kyun nahi?
items.topic: Embedding search finds meaning but can miss exact strings such as an error code; hybrid retrieval adds BM25 keyword search and merges both result lists with rank fusion; Anthropic reports top-20 retrieval failures falling from 5.7% to 2.9% (49%) with contextual embeddings plus contextual BM25 and to 1.9% with reranking.
items.hook_formula: Hook A (stake, contradiction, trap, open loop)

items.title: Interview: Prompt badla, ek jagah behtar hua, doosri jagah toota. Kaise pakdoge?
items.topic: Keep a fixed set of test cases (typical, edge and nasty inputs) with automatic grading and rerun all of them after every prompt or model change, so you see what got worse as well as what got better; use a different model as grader than the one being graded.
items.hook_formula: Hook A (stake, contradiction, trap, open loop)

items.title: Interview: AI app ka pehla word 8 second baad aata hai. Latency kaise kam karoge?
items.topic: Latency has two parts: time to first token (when the user sees the first word) and total generation time; reduce it by choosing a smaller, faster model, trimming prompt and output length, and streaming so the first words appear while the rest is still being written.
items.hook_formula: Hook A (stake, contradiction, trap, open loop)

items.title: Interview: Agent ko sirf padhna tha, DELETE ka hak bhi mila tha. Permissions kaise design karoge?
items.topic: OWASP LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency: excessive functionality, excessive permissions and excessive autonomy; fix with minimum tools, least-privilege permissions, human approval for destructive actions and authorization enforced in downstream systems, not in the LLM.

items.title: Interview: Support chatbot ke liye bada model ya chhota? Decide kaise karoge?
items.topic: Choosing a model by evaluation: own test set, efficiency-first or capability-first start, effort as a lever before switching models, routing easy queries to a cheap model and hard ones to a stronger model (Anthropic: choosing the right model).

items.title: Prompt caching se AI ka jawab badal jata hai? Aur lambi chat idle chhodo to?
items.topic: Claude Code v2.1.299 (14 Oct 2026) compacts a 200K+ token chat idle for about 54 minutes before its one-hour prompt cache expires; Anthropic's caching docs say caching has no effect on output generation, the answer is identical, it only reuses the processed prompt prefix (read 0.1x, 5-min write 1.25x).
items.hook_idea: Interview-framed belief: 'Caching ka matlab AI ne yaad rakh liya, jawab alag aayega?' then the doc line that it is identical.

items.title: Safety check crash hua, phir bhi AI ka kaam ho gaya: ab fail hone par block karo
items.topic: Claude Code v2.1.295 (8 Oct 2026) added onFailure: block for command and HTTP hooks: a hook that cannot start, times out or exits unexpectedly now blocks the action instead of letting it through (fail closed vs fail open).
items.hook_idea: Your guard crashed and the agent still deleted the file: before/after of an open door vs a locked door.

items.title: Ek line likho, agent poori machine ka exploded drawing bana de: anatomy skill
items.topic: Agent skill 'anatomy' (GitHub wheresryan22/anatomy, MIT, created 8 Oct 2026) makes a coding agent build an interactive exploded-view SVG of a system from one prompt; all claims are the author's own; HELD for owner call on fast star growth (about 14.9k in 9 days), no star count on screen. Backup item: Anthropic RCT (29 Jan 2026) on asking concept questions vs delegating.
items.hook_idea: One sentence in, a part-by-part exploded drawing of a rate limiter out.

items.title: Context mein kya-kya jata hai? Context ke 5 sources
items.topic: Context is everything in the model's window: system prompt, tools, examples, message history and external data; each source must stay lean (Anthropic, effective context engineering).
items.hook_idea: Model ko jawab dene se pehle kya-kya dikhta hai? then 5 sources as 5 boxes filling a window.

items.title: Context compaction kya hai? Lambi chat ko chhota kaise karte hain
items.topic: Compaction means summarising a conversation nearing the window limit and restarting a new context window with the summary, plus low-risk pruning such as dropping redundant tool outputs (Anthropic, effective context engineering). Angle differs from q16 (sliding window and vector DB).
items.hook_idea: Compaction kya hota hai? long chat shrinks into a summary card.

items.title: RAG kya hai? AI ko apni notebook dekhne do
items.topic: RAG retrieves relevant information from a knowledge base and appends it to the user's prompt; chunks are embedded, the most similar are fetched at question time (Lewis et al. 2020 abstract; Anthropic contextual retrieval). Skips D5 second reel for now.
items.hook_idea: RAG kya hai? question goes to a shelf, 3 pages come back, join the prompt.

items.title: Interview: Poora PDF context mein daal doon ya RAG banaun?
items.topic: If the knowledge base is under about 200,000 tokens, Anthropic says you can include all of it in the prompt and RAG is not needed, with prompt caching cutting latency by more than 2x and cost by up to 90%; above that, retrieve chunks.
items.hook_idea: Someone built a full RAG stack for a 40-page handbook that fit in one prompt.

items.title: Interview: Agent loop mein fas gaya, ye kaise rokoge? (Onit job post)
items.topic: Agents need stopping conditions such as a maximum number of iterations, ground truth from the environment at each step and human checkpoints (Anthropic, building effective agents). Company hook limited to what the job post says: Onit's AI Engineer post lists agent loops and failure handling; it is a job post, not an interview question.
items.hook_idea: Onit ke AI Engineer job post mein agent loops aur failure handling likha hai; tum agent ko kaise rokoge? (company=Onit)

items.title: Interview: Chatbot ne galat jawab diya, pata kaise chalega kyun?
items.topic: A trace shows the full path of one request as spans (name, start, end, parent) so you see which step ran and how long it took; for LLM apps it shows retrieval, prompt and tool steps (OpenTelemetry traces concept page).
items.hook_idea: Interviewer ne poocha: Production chatbot ne galat jawab diya, tumhe kaise pata chalega kyun?

items.title: Interview: Chatbot ne galat jawab diya, par kal ka kuch record nahi. Debug kaise karoge?
items.topic: When an LLM app gives a wrong answer, the final answer alone cannot tell you why; a trace, one record of the whole request with each step's input, output, time and tokens, shows which step went wrong.
items.office_note: approved by the owner as q27 on 2026-10-17; renamed to q104 because office ids start at 101

items.title: Chhota jawab padhne se bill kam hota hai? cc-stretch: click karo, jawab khulta hai
items.topic: cc-stretch is a Claude Code plugin that shows short replies where each linked phrase expands in place when clicked; you read less, but by the author's own statement you do not pay less, because each reply costs about the same tokens.

items.title: Model pichli chat kyun bhool jata hai? AI ki memory notebook
items.topic: The context window is a small, limited desk that gets cluttered as it fills; agent memory means writing notes to storage outside the window and reading them back when needed, and the memory tool is that notebook: a /memories folder your own app manages.

items.title: How a model learns: forward pass, loss, gradient descent
items.topic: Day 1 of 150 Days of AI: a one-weight model learns marks = 2 x hours by forward pass, mean squared error, gradient descent; learning rate 0.5 diverges; an LLM trains the same loop.

items.title: Train, validation and test: three piles of data
items.topic: Day 2 of 150 Days of AI: train, validation and test sets and their three jobs; a model that memorises scores 100 percent on train and 72 on validation; validation chooses the model; the test set is opened once; peeking at it turns it into a validation set.

items.title: Interview: Temperature, Top-K aur Top-P ka difference batao
items.topic: Top-K keeps a fixed count of the most probable next words, Top-P keeps the smallest set reaching a cumulative probability threshold, and Temperature reshapes the probability distribution.

items.title: Interview: Prompt mein examples dene se model hamesha behtar hota hai?
items.topic: Examples in a prompt show the model the shape of the answer and the allowed labels, so they usually help; but every example costs tokens on every request, a one-sided set or a bad order pulls the answer, and the only way to know is to measure with and without.
items.hook_formula: interviewer_asked: one complete question of 11 words in plain words

items.title: Interview: Temperature, top-k aur top-p teeno laga diye. Output pe kaun sa asar karta hai?
items.topic: Temperature, top-k and top-p do three different jobs: top-k (by count) and top-p (by total chance) cut the list of next words, temperature only reshapes the chances of the words that are left, and changing one changes what another keeps.
items.office_note: version B of question 105 for the trial test T01; a repeat on purpose, not a new question

items.title: Overfitting: when a model memorises instead of learning
items.topic: Overfitting is a model matching its training data so closely (noise included) that it fails on new data; the sign is a training error near zero with a much bigger error on new data, and the cure is a simpler model or more data, judged on data it has not seen.

items.title: Interview: Model ko 'step by step socho' bolna har baar kaam karta hai?
items.topic: Chain-of-thought (asking the model to write its reasoning steps before the answer) helps on multi-step maths and logic, but gives little on easy or non-reasoning questions, costs extra output on every request, and is often unnecessary on reasoning models that already think internally: test it on your own questions.

items.title: Interview: System prompt aur user prompt mein conflict ho to model kiski sunta hai?
items.topic: Models are trained to give the developer's system prompt more authority than the user's message (OpenAI's Model Spec: developer messages have greater authority), so usually the system prompt wins; but it is a strong instruction, not a lock, so anything that must never happen is enforced in code outside the model.

items.title: An LLM is a next-word predictor: watch the guesses
items.topic: An LLM writes by repeatedly making a list of possible next words with odds, picking one and adding it; the answer is built one word at a time.

items.title: Interview: Model ne confidently galat fact bol diya. Hallucination kyun hoti hai, aur kaise kam karoge?
items.topic: Hallucination: the model predicts likely words and training and grading reward guessing; reduce with RAG, allowing I don't know, and output checks.

items.title: Interview: Open source model use karoge ya closed API? Decide kaise karoge?
items.topic: Decide on data privacy and control, cost at your own request volume (an API is pay per use, self-hosting is a fixed server bill plus someone to run it) and the licence terms, not on benchmark scores alone; start with an API and move when volume or privacy demands it.
